title: 11.1 A 256-Element Ka-Band CMOS Phased-Array Receiver Using Switch-Type Quadrature-Hybrid-First Architecture for Small Satellite Constellations
problem: Small satellite constellations require flexible receiver support for diverse mission profiles and power budgets: 10s-of-kg satellites need low power for single-polarized signals; 100s-of-kg satellites need to support high-speed dual-polarization simultaneously from different sources; conventional receivers are fixed to single or dual polarization with high power overhead.
motivation: Small satellite constellations deploy many compact satellites in LEO for redundancy and cost-effective global coverage; diverse satellite sizes require adaptable RF front-ends.
method: The receiver uses 256 antenna elements arranged in a phased array—a technique where multiple antennas work together and their signal timing is adjusted to focus reception in particular directions. It operates in the Ka-band microwave frequencies. The design positions switches and quadrature hybrids (circuits that split signals into two versions shifted 90 degrees apart) early in the signal chain, allowing the same hardware to flexibly switch between receiving single circular-polarized waves (where the wave rotates in one direction), dual circular-polarized waves (receiving two circular rotations simultaneously), or linear-polarized waves (where the wave vibrates in a fixed plane)—different encoding schemes satellites use depending on their mission.
key_novelty: The switch-type quadrature-hybrid-first design enables flexible polarization switching without duplicating hardware, reducing power consumption by 50% when operating in single-polarization mode.
contributions: Switch-type quadrature hybrid for flexible polarization modes
Support for dual-independent signal reception (UT + ground station)
primary_theme: Flexible Ka-band phased-array receiver for diverse satellite missions
